newsitem.title: USA: US disappointed by Japan decision on brake parts.
newsitem.headline: US disappointed by Japan decision on brake parts.

text.p: U.S. trade officials said Wednesday they were disappointed that Japan's Ministry of Transport rejected a petition by U.S. auto parts manufacturers seeking greater deregulation of brake parts.

"The U.S.-Japan auto agreement calls for opening the Japanese auto parts market to the greatest extent possible consistent with safety considerations," U.S. Trade Representative Designate Charlene Barshefsky said in a statement.
"The decision of the Japanese government is a move in exactly the wrong direction and only makes deregulation of Japan's garage system even more important," she added.
She called rejection of the petition "a step backwards" and said the U.S. would pursue the matter with the Japanese government.
A 1995 trade agreement calls for greater deregulation of Japan's lucrative auto parts markets and rule changes that would allow more independent repair shops to operate.
The USTR said new regulations on car repair shops are due to be published by February 23.
